The highest power coefficient of 0.4218 was obtained using the SST turbulence model with the fine mesh.
The power coefficients obtained from the standard k-epsilon model were 15-20% lower than the SST model.
The medium mesh with the SST model provided the best balance of accuracy and computational cost.
The torque coefficient increased with increasing tip speed ratio, but dropped drastically after a tip speed ratio of 5, which the k-epsilon model failed to capture.
The straight blade tidal turbine had three blades with a radius of 7.4 m and used a NACA 0018 airfoil.
The root airfoil chord length was 1 m, the tip airfoil chord length was 360 mm, the root airfoil twist was 16°, and the tip airfoil twist was 4°.
The mesh independency study was performed by developing three different meshes: coarse, medium, and fine, for both the k-epsilon and SST turbulence models.
The SST medium mesh offered the best level of accuracy regarding computational costs.
The standard k-epsilon model under-predicted the power coefficients due to its poor performance in near-wall regions and adverse pressure gradients.
The straight blade tidal turbine produced a maximum power of 366 kW and a power coefficient of 0.4028.
The mesh resolution and the turbulence model selection had a significant impact on the power coefficient results.
The highest lift coefficient of 0.182 was observed at the 0.5 blade span location.
Positive blade tip vortices were observed on the pressure side of the blade due to high turbulence intensities.
The fluid velocity expanded as it passed through the turbine, contributing to the maximum efficiency.
The convergence condition was determined with a margin of error less than 10^-5, and each case study required at least 3 hours of simulation time.
